name: Aqua Park Shinagawa
desc: Dolphin performance with lights and music. More of a show than quiet viewing.

name: teamLab Planets
desc: Barefoot walk through water, digital koi, flower garden. About 1.5–2 hours. Best hands-on pick for a 10-year-old. Timed tickets.

name: teamLab Borderless
desc: Shoes on, no map, maze of light rooms plus Athletic Forest. 2–3 hours. Dry floors. Check Tuesday closures.

name: New Year Kabuki
desc: January program; English audio guide for rent. Tickets on sale from 13 Dec 2026. Afternoon-friendly for adults.

name: Ryoko Moriyama
desc: Folk / pop concert at the Budokan. Ticketed; check official sale.

name: Yomiuri Nippon Symphony
desc: Classical evening at 19:00 in Ikebukuro. Part of Tokyo performing-music listings.

name: ORANGE RANGE
desc: J-rock / pop concert. Ticketed; confirm the official sale.

name: LiSA
desc: J-pop / anime-song live, two nights. Sells out. New waterfront arena at Aomi.

name: TCB comedy
desc: Stand-up bill; some nights are English-friendly. Confirm the January lineup.

name: Musée d’Orsay exhibition
desc: “Joy of living” works from the Musée d’Orsay. Indoor adult option next to Ueno Zoo.

name: Yokohama Illumination
desc: City-wide winter lights. Yorunoyo’s big 2026 show ends 30 Dec, but waterfront lights continue into February. Free. About 30 min from Tokyo Station.

name: Cup Noodles Museum
desc: Make your own cup. High school and under free entry; factory extras cost extra. 10:00–18:00. Next to Cosmo World.

name: Yokohama Cosmo World
desc: Ferris wheel and rides. Pay per ride or pass. Easy with Cup Noodles and Red Brick Warehouse.

name: Hakkeijima Sea Paradise
desc: Large aquarium, dolphin and beluga shows, amusement park. Full-day kid trip. Winter outdoor rides may pause in wind.

name: Yokohama Chinatown
desc: Food streets, Hikawa Maru, Landmark Tower. Chinese New Year festival starts 20 Jan — after this week.

name: Joma Shinji archery
desc: Archers shoot a target painted with “demon.” Samurai-era New Year rite. Free to watch at the main shrine.

name: Hatsu Kagura
desc: First kagura dance of the year. Small local shrine ceremony.

name: Dai-shime Festival
desc: Giant shimenawa rope offering in centipede form, for harvest and safety.

name: Hon Ebisu
desc: Ebisu festival: fuku-musume in costume hand out lucky mochi and sake charms.

name: Shio matsuri (Sakanoshita)
desc: Sea rite for safe fishing and navigation. Cold outdoor morning — dress warm.

name: Shio kagura (Zaimokuza)
desc: Kagura on the sand for sea safety. Same morning as the Sakanoshita rite.

name: Great Buddha (Kotoku-in)
desc: Kamakura’s bronze Daibutsu. Easy day from Tokyo (~1 hour). Combine with a dated shrine rite.

name: Hasedera
desc: Kannon temple with hillside gardens and a view of Yuigahama. Next to the Great Buddha.

name: Edo-Tokyo Museum
desc: Reopened after renovation. Life-size Nihonbashi and Edo streets. Pair with sumo. Maruyama Okyo special through 24 Jan 2027.

name: National Museum of Nature and Science
desc: Dinosaurs, blue whale, two galleries. Best indoor kid museum this week. School-age entry is free. 11 Jan holiday should be open.

name: Tokyo National Museum
desc: Largest collection in Japan: armor, sculpture, lacquer. The Genji special starts 19 Jan, after this week.

name: Mori Art Museum
desc: Contemporary art and Tokyo City View. Easy with Midtown skating and teamLab Borderless.

name: Tokyo Toy Museum
desc: Wooden toys and play rooms in a former elementary school. Hands-on, 1–2 hours. Closed Thursdays — so closed 7 Jan 2027.

name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
desc: Showa street downstairs and regional ramen counters. Pair with the skate center.

name: Kamakura National Treasure Museum
desc: Temple sculptures and treasures, often without glass. Small visit next to the shrine.
